agent: wave diplomatic-state, brief D (the diplomacy screen, its list half)
question: What CDiplomacyView does with the left half of tfh/interface/country_diplomacy.gui: construction, show, update, the five tabs, the nine sort buttons, a CCountrylistItem row and its figures, choosing a country, the three toggles and the mode arrows, and the tooltips of the list's elements.

addresses.name: CDiplomacyView::CDiplomacyView
addresses.comment: **The diplomacy screen's constructor.** Extent 0x77D090..0x77D97C, `ret 8`, nothing in ECX. One caller, 0x659878 inside CInGameIdler::Update's view setup, after `operator new(0x560)`; the result goes into the in-game screen's view vector (+0xD00) at index 0. Calls CCountryView::CCountryView (0x2EB040) with the windows 'country_diplomacy' and 'topcolor_diplomacy' and view index 0, writes the vftable (0x15DABE4), sets the selected country (+0x1DC/+0x1E0) to the played country (game state +0xC30/+0xC34), +0xBC to the null date, the sort flag +0x4D8 to 0, and lays out 23 observer glues - the checkbox glue at +0xE0 (handler 0x38E290) and button glues at +0x100, +0x12C, +0x158, +0x184, +0x1B0, +0x1E4, +0x210, +0x23C, +0x268, +0x294, +0x2C0, +0x2EC, +0x34C..+0x4AC (every 0x2C) and +0x534; which element each is attached to is CDiplomacyView::BuildWidgets (0x381310), which it tail-calls.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0x77D090..0x77D97C: `ret 8` at 0x77D97C is the only exit; vftable store `mov [esi], 0x15DABE4` at 0x77D12F (findRefs --vftable CDiplomacyView, the only constructor-shaped write); call site 0x659878 pushes ebx (the idler) and the 0x560-byte block. Wrong if 0x659878's ebx is not the in-game idler.

addresses.name: CDiplomacyView::ScalarDeletingDestructor
addresses.comment: Slot 1: the destructor body (0x37D9B0), then `free` when bit 0 of `flags` is set.
addresses.evidence: vtable.py: CDiplomacyView slot 1 = 0x77D980; body is `call 0x77D9B0; test flags,1; free`, `ret 4`.

addresses.name: CDiplomacyView::~CDiplomacyView
addresses.comment: The destructor body. Empties `diplostatus_list` and `drift_list`, empties each faction box, frees the faction box, faction sort window and continent button lists (+0x31C, +0x32C, +0x33C) and the CGM widgets (0x38F6A0), the faction sort button list (+0x508), the alignment markers (+0xC0) and the country list (+0xD0), puts CButtonObserver's vftable back on every glue, and then destroys the two windows as CCountryView. Ghidra's RTTI pass labels it a constructor; it is not - it restores base vftables and frees. Extent 0x77D9B0..0x77DF37, bare `ret`.
addresses.evidence: Called only from slot 1 (0x77D986). Writes CCountryView::vftable over the object at the end and frees every list the constructor created. Bare ret at 0x77DF37 then int3.

addresses.name: CDiplomacyView::Show
addresses.comment: **Slot 2: the screen is shown.** In order: +0x518 = 0; **if exactly one province is selected on the map and it has an owner, that owner becomes the selected country** (CInGameIdler::GetSelectedProvince, slot 39, then CDiplomacyView::SelectCountry on the province's +0x32C owner); every selected object of type 0, 1 or 2 (army, navy, air) is copied to +0x4DC..+0x4E8 with its name (for the diplomatic actions; not followed); **if the country list (+0xD0) is empty, the All tab's handler runs** (0x38C900) - so the first opening shows All and later openings keep whatever tab and order were last made; then RebuildAlignmentMarkers, UpdateFactionBoxes(0), RefreshCountryInfo (0x388F70), RebuildActionList for the selected country, RebuildDecisionList, both windows shown, slot 11 (the automation line); in `country_info` the windows `goal_list_window` and `relation_list_window` hidden and `diplostatus_list` shown (so the panel always reopens on Info); `decisions_listbox` and `diploaction_list` shown in a normal game and hidden in a custom game (g_CustomGameSettings first byte); finally 0x38E3D0 (CGM widgets). **The country list box is not rebuilt here**: rows keep the threat figure they were made with.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled 0x77DF40 and disassembly 0x77DFE4..0x77E00A: game state +0xBE8 slot 39 (0x9C), `cmp [eax+0x330],0`, `add eax,0x32C; push eax; mov ecx,ebx; call 0x784A30`. The empty-list test is `param_1[0x36] == 0` (+0xD8, the list's count) before `call 0x78C900`. Wrong if +0xD8 is not the count of the +0xD0 list - the tab handlers write it as such.

addresses.name: CDiplomacyView::Update
addresses.comment: **Slot 6: the per-frame update while the screen is open**, called through CInGameIdler_UpdateOpenView (0x251D30) from CInGameIdler::Update. In order: UpdateFactionBoxes(0); RefreshDriftList (0x384610); when the clock (+0xBDC) has passed +0xBC, RebuildAlignmentMarkers and +0xBC = clock + ALIGNMENT_INTERVAL(whole) * 24 hours; every `diploaction_list` row's slot 11; **every row of `country_listbox` whose window is visible (+0x5B) gets CCountrylistItem::UpdateResourceIcons, and a row whose country owns no province (that function answering false) is taken out of the country list** (unlinked and freed, or marked +0x10 when the list's +0xDC lock is set) - when any was, the list box and the markers are rebuilt; `surrender_progress` set (brief E); when +0x504 differs from the player's threat from its HighestThreat, RefreshCountryInfo (0x388F70); every `decisions_listbox` row's slot 8 while that list is shown; `trade_automate_checkbox` and its label shown/hidden by the custom-game byte and the checkbox's state from the local player's +0x34; **the seven resource sort buttons shown in a normal game and hidden in a custom game**; then 0x38EC90 (CGM). Threat, name and flag of a row are never refreshed here.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled 0x77E530; refresh timer at 0x77E5E4 `mov eax,[eax+0xBDC]; cmp eax,[edi+0xBC]; jle`; the row loop tests `[[row+0x20]+0x5B]` before calling 0x785910 (short-circuit), removal at 0x77E880..0x77E8CC. Bare ret 0x77F488. That it runs every frame rests on CInGameIdler::Update calling 0x251D30 unconditionally at 0x656465 - `inferred` for 'every frame'.

addresses.name: CDiplomacyView::BuildTooltip
addresses.signature: GuiTooltipText* __thiscall CDiplomacyView::BuildTooltip(CDiplomacyView* this, GuiTooltipText* out, CGuiObject* element)
addresses.comment: **Slot 10: every tooltip on the diplomacy screen that is not the element's own.** Reached through CInGameIdler_ViewTooltip. Dispatch order: in a custom game the CGM elements first (CGM_TOOLTIP_NEUTRALITY, _LEAVE_FACTION, _REJOIN_FACTION, _ALREADY_IN_FACTION, _FACTION_ALIGN); `faction_button` (FACTION_MEMBER_OF / LEAVE_FACTION_INTENTION); `highest_threat_flag`, `label_highest_threat_value`, `label_highest_threat` (DIP_HIGHEST_THREAT_TOOLTIP with COUNTRY and VAL = +0x504 to one decimal, delayed DIP_HIGHEST_THREAT_TOOLTIP_DELAYED); `alignment_button` (BuildFactionIntentionTooltip); `faction_symbol_button`; `faction_symbol_big_button` (the faction's slot 6 text, delayed 0x522AF0); `victory_progress`; `surrender_progress`; `label_neutrality_value`, `label_our_neutrality_value` (modifier contributors). Then the lists, each asked whether it owns the element: **`country_listbox` rows - only the seven resource icons answer (CCountrylistItem::IsResourceIcon) and get CCountrylistItem::BuildTradeSurplusTooltip**; `diploaction_list` rows; `domestictext_relationlist` rows; `decisions_listbox` rows while shown (CDecisionEntry::OwnsElement/BuildTooltip); `goals_by_us` and `goals_at_us` entries (CGoalOverviewEntry_BuildTooltip). **Nothing here answers the five tab buttons, the nine sort buttons, the three toggles, a row's flag, name, threat or checkbox**, and the .gui gives all of them empty tooltips. Extent 0x77F490..0x7810E3, `ret 8`.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled 0x77F490; the row loop at 0x780A80..0x780ACA calls `[row+0x1C]` slot 22 (0x58) then `mov ecx,edi; call 0x786690`. The element-name compares are literal strings in the body. Positive control for the negative about tabs and sort buttons: the same dispatch does answer the seven icons; wrong if some other route (the element's own declared tooltip) supplied text - the .gui declares `tooltip = ""` for all of them.

addresses.name: CDiplomacyView::Rebuild
addresses.comment: Slot 0. Sets +0xB8, runs CCountryView::Rebuild (which remakes the main window, so `country_listbox` comes back empty), then RebuildAlignmentMarkers and BuildWidgets, clears +0xB8 and answers what BuildWidgets answered. **It does not refill the country list box**, and Show refills it only when the country list is empty - so after this the rows stay empty until a tab or sort button is pressed (inferred from the absence of any list box rebuild on this path; who calls slot 0 was not read).
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0x7812D0..0x781306: `mov byte [edi+0xB8],1; call 0x6EB3D0; test al,al; jne` -> `call 0x783C50; call 0x781310; mov byte [edi+0xB8],0`.

addresses.name: CDiplomacyView::BuildWidgets
addresses.comment: **Binds every element of the screen's left half to its handler, and makes the widgets the .gui declares outside the main window.** (1) a `faction_box_window` per faction in the game state's faction list (+0xCE4) at `faction_start` + n * `faction_offset`, each with a CFactionWindow glue, `faction_symbol_button` and `name` (the triangle; later work). (2) **a `diplomacy_faction_sort_window` per faction whose slot 7 says it is a real faction** (CNullFaction answers no), at `diplomacy_sort_faction_start` (56,75) + n * `diplomacy_sort_faction_offset` (101,0), its `faction_symbol_big_button` given the sprite 'GFX_sort_' + the faction's key and the faction's slot 6 text, glued to 0x38FCF0 (lists that faction's members), kept in +0x32C and +0x508, and named key + '_sort'. (3) UpdateFactionBoxes(0). (4) **a `continent_button` per continent of the map's list (CMap +0x2A30) except `lake` and `greenland`**, text = the continent's slot 6 text, named 'cont_button_' + its index, glued to 0x38FD00 (lists that continent), placed from `continent_offset` (57,133) in steps of `continent_start` (100,0), wrapping to the next line 20 down (`continent_end` y) at x >= 356 (`continent_end` x) - so the file's two names are swapped, as its own comments say. (5) observers: `majors_button` +0x100 (0x383F20), `neighbours_button` +0x12C (0x384140), `unaligned_button` +0x158 (0x3842E0), `self_button` +0x184 (0x384560), `all_button` +0x1B0 (0x38C900) - all inside the window `alignment`; `toggle_diploview_button_goals` +0x23C (0x388870), `_country` +0x268 (0x388450), `_relation` +0x294 (0x388610) inside `country_info`; `sortby_nation_button` +0x1E4 and `sortby_relation_button` +0x210 inside `relation_list_window`; `sortby_name_button` +0x34C (0x38CE50), `sortby_threat_button` +0x378 (0x38D130), the seven resource buttons +0x3A4..+0x4AC (0x38D620..0x38D680); `trade_automate_checkbox` +0xE0 (0x38E290), it and its label shown in a normal game and hidden in a custom one. (6) FillCountryInfoHeader (0x384E30), 0x38E3D0, and slot 30 of the window with 'diplomacy_view'. Extent 0x781310..0x7831D2; the bare `ret` at 0x781B0E is the early exit when a faction window cannot be made (trap 3).
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0x781310..0x7831D2 (scratchpad d781310.txt): each element name pushed, then `lea edx,[edi+X]` and the found element's +0x48 observer list slot 1 - the X per button listed. Continent placement 0x78200D..0x7823FA; 0x486DB0 answers false for 'lake' and 'greenland'. Handlers read off the constructor's glue stores. Wrong if `[edi+X]` is not the glue the constructor filled - each X matches a constructor store exactly.

addresses.name: CDiplomacyView::UpdateFactionBoxes
addresses.comment: Each frame (from Update) and on Show: for every faction box (+0x31C) sets its two `victory_progress` bars to the faction's victory-point share / 1000; and when the faction's members changed (CFaction +0x38, cleared here), the view is rebuilding (+0xB8), `force` is set, or the box's count differs from the members (plus, in a custom game, its CGM extra list), moves the box to `faction_start` + n * `faction_offset`, empties its `faction_box` and adds a `faction_member_entry` per member (0x3835F0). The faction triangle's boxes; later work, read only so far.
addresses.evidence: Decompiled 0x7831E0; two exits `ret 8` (0x7835D1, 0x7835E6). Likely, not confirmed: the box/member reading is from the decompiled C only.

addresses.name: CCountrylistItem::UpdateResourceIcons
addresses.comment: **What the seven icons of a row show.** Answers false and does nothing when the country owns no province. Otherwise, for each of `icon_supplies`, `icon_fuel`, `icon_money`, `icon_oil`, `icon_metal`, `icon_energy`, `icon_raremet`, the country's **day's balance of that good** (the ledger sum GetDailyBalance computes - inline for supplies, fuel, money and oil, by a call for metal, energy and rare materials) decides the icon's tint through its drawable's slot 68: **balance above zero: (1.0, 1.0, 1.0, 1.0) and 0; zero or below: (1.0, 0.5, 0.5, 1.0) and 1** - a light red. Then all seven are shown (slot 13) in a normal game and hidden (slot 14) in a custom game. Called on construction, when a row is shown, and every frame for visible rows from Update. **There is no figure on a row; the resources are only icons.**
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0x7859A0..: CColor locals built from 0x171DBAC (1.0f) and 0x15AB304 (0.5f); energy at 0x785DF1 `call GetDailyBalance(5)`, 0x785DF6 `cmp [eax],0; jg white`. Extent 0x785910..0x78621A `ret 4`; the `ret 4` at 0x785957 is the no-province exit (trap 3). That the four floats are red, green, blue, alpha in that order is inferred.

addresses.signature: GuiTooltipText* __thiscall CCountrylistItem::BuildTradeSurplusTooltip(CCountrylistItem* this, GuiTooltipText* out, CGuiObject* element)
addresses.comment: **The tooltip of a row's resource icon.** `this` is the row (ECX: its window +0x20 and country +0x2C); `out` a 0x5C-byte GuiTooltipText it initialises (three empty strings, position 0, below 1); `element` the icon hovered. For whichever of the seven it is, the country's day's balance of that good b (thousandths; energy and money by the inline ledger sum, the other five by CCountry::GetDailyBalance - supplies and fuel without convoyed_in, as that function has it): **b < 0 gives DIP_NO_SURPLUS with VAL = -b, b >= 0 gives DIP_SURPLUS with VAL = b**; NAME = CountryNameOfTag(country), RES = the localised ENERGY_IRO, RAREMAT_IRO, METAL_IRO, CRUDE_OIL_IRO, SUPPLIES_IRO, FUEL_IRO or MONEY_IRO, and VAL = b / 1000 through single precision and FormatFloat(2) - '%.2f', rounded. English: '$NAME$ is in deficit of §Y$VAL$§W $RES$ each day.' / '$NAME$ is producing a surplus of §Y$VAL$§W $RES$ each day.' Only `text` is filled. **At exactly zero the icon is red and the tooltip says surplus.** Extent 0x786690..0x788414, `ret 8`, one caller (0x780ABD in CDiplomacyView::BuildTooltip).
addresses.evidence: Disassembly 0x786690..: `mov edi,ecx` then `[edi+0x20]`, `add edi,0x2C; call CCountryTag::GetCountry`; out at [ebp+8] (+0x10/+0x14/+0x2C/+0x30/+0x48/+0x4C/+0x54 cleared, +0x58 = 1); element compared with `[ebp+0xC]`. Tests: energy `jns 0x786B16` (surplus), raremet/metal/oil/supplies/fuel `jge` after `call 0x4F18A0`, money `jns 0x788246`; deficit arms `xorps xmm0,[0x160A380]` (sign flip) before `call 0xA5AEC0` with `push 2`. Call site 0x780AB2: `push eax(element); push ecx(out); mov ecx,edi(row)`.
addresses.revises: Was `Hoi3CString* __stdcall BuildTradeSurplusTooltip(Hoi3CString* out, int unknown)`, `likely`, receiver unknown. It is a CCountrylistItem method: the row arrives in ECX, `out` is a GuiTooltipText and the second argument is the hovered element. The comment now gives the texts, the zero case and the number format.

struct_fields.name: sort_flag
struct_fields.comment: **One direction flag for all nine sort buttons**: each press flips it and then sorts by it (1: Z-A, highest threat, largest surplus first; 0 the reverse). Zeroed only by the constructor, so the first press of any sort button gives the flag-1 order.
struct_fields.evidence: dispscan for +0x4D8 over 0x77B000..0x790000: one write in the constructor (0x77D86E), the rest in 0x38CE50, 0x38D130, 0x38D690.
